title: Kansas City musicians, Earl Hines on the radio, and the Subway
summary: He names Baby Lovett, Julia Lee and Mary Lou Williams, describes musicians gathering in the hotel lobby to hear Hines, and says the sessions were in a basement club called the Subway.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Well, Jo Jones was playing then. Was he playing --
No, I didn't meet Jo back in there. I didn't meet -- you know who I -- Baby Lovett.
Baby Lovett, Julia Lee, Mary Lou Williams, all the greatest array of -- and it was the greatest array of musicians in the world. Right there.
You know? And what they would do, like I said, the guys would come in, they would sit up in the
lobby, and at 11:30 -- I guess it was 11:30 at night, that lobby would be full, listening to Earl Hines, coming from the Grand Terrace.
Where did these sessions take place in Kansas City?

They -- in a little joint called the Subway. And it was down in the basement, it was down in the basement. It was a restaurant on top of something, and then right down in the basement, they had this subway. It was like a little club, a little club. And this is where they would take place.
